quest.title: The Meaning of Meaningless Waiting
quest.description: The village guardian who has lost his Vision seems to have forgotten why he had remained there in the first place...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x800, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.title: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia

talks.objective: Go to Konda Village and find out what happened

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see, where's the person Ayaka told us about...

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: Why are you doing this? Why leave all of a sudden, after all these years?

dialogues.speaker: Kenjirou
dialogues.text: Precisely, it's much too sudden. We've had no time to prepare...

dialogues.speaker: Kenjirou
dialogues.text: The children are desperate for you to take them out to play... Please, we urge you to reconsider!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That must be the guy Ayaka told us about. Let's go over and see!

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: Ah... You must also be here to try and convince Tejima to stay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's happened?

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: Tejima has protected this place ever since he arrived here 30 years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: Keeping out the Treasure Hoarders, fending off any monsters that draw near, resolving quarrels between the villagers... he has put an enormous amount of work into looking after this place, and we all think the world of him.

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: But now, all of a sudden, he says he plans to leave us... We can't help but wonder — was it something we did?

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: We will gladly apologize if that's the case... All we want is for him to stay...

dialogues.speaker: Kenjirou
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So why the change?

dialogues.speaker: Kenjirou
dialogues.text: If you want my opinion, something to do with the Vision Hunt Decree.

dialogues.speaker: Kenjirou
dialogues.text: It's clear that Tejima had done nothing wrong. And still they confiscated his Vision. After that... he became a completely different person.

dialogues.speaker: Kenjirou
dialogues.text: I can't claim to fully understand it, but I could tell that he'd lost something very important to him. He went off on a walk, alone, circled the village a few times, and then out of the blue, he announced that he was going to leave and become a wanderer.

dialogues.speaker: Kenjirou
dialogues.text: Truth be told, we aren't sure whether trying to keep him here is the right thing to do. But equally... it doesn't feel right to let him leave when he's in this state. He's a lost soul.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like he's a well-respected guy around here.

talks.objective: Talk to Tejima and find out what happened

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You must be Tejima? So, what's made you wanna up and leave all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Me...? I... It's not a question of why I want to leave... but a question of... what reason I would have to stay.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've lived here for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Everyone depends on you.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: True... but that's not why I chose to stay here...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: ...and what made me want to come here 30 years ago? And why have I never wanted to leave in all that time?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: *sigh* I don't have answers to those questions, because I can't remember anymore. Ever since they took my Vision away, it's like... a slice of my memory is gone.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: In the past, I knew I wanted to stay here... but whatever resolve I had then, it's gone now. So I thought, what's to stop me from moving around instead? The emptiness inside me will be there either way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... Well, in that case, if we help you rediscover the reason you chose to stay, you won't need to leave anymore, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... But if you can't remember anything, it's not gonna be easy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Maybe if you just try a little harder to remember, then... it'll all come flooding back?

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: Oh, that reminds me... Last time I brought Tejima some fruit, I do believe I saw him writing in a diary.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: ...I keep a diary? If you say so... I honestly can't seem to remember.

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, you do! And what's more, I remember you saying at the time that you wanted to make a note of a few interesting things — things which would prove very important at a later date.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Perfect! So, if we wanna keep Tejima from leaving, we just need to find his diary. It must be around here somewhere, let's take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: If you don't mind, we will leave you to find the diary... we should head back to the village to inform the others of Tejima's situation.

talks.objective: Find the clues to Tejima's memory

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This looks like Tejima's diary alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see what we have here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Today, the villagers and I got together to cook Dry-Braised Salted Fish. I messed up and burned mine a little, so I had to pretend that it was Black Snakehead instead."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Today, I helped rescue a kid who had fallen in the water. After I pulled him out, he told me that his best friend, Banbu, was still in the water. I searched the water the whole afternoon before finding out that Banbu was the name of his pet crab."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "I went kite-flying today. The string broke, so I chased after it as fast as I could. I soon realized I was never going to get it back, so I just found somewhere to sit and watch as it flew away into the distance."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Seems like your average diary of daily village life...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait — there's more!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "I went to pray at the shrine again today, and stayed there a while. The omamori you gave me has faded a little, but it is still my most treasured possession..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that's the kind of info we're looking for! Time to pay a visit to the shrine!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the omamori Tejima wrote about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Interesting... looking at the color and the design, Paimon would've thought it belonged to a child...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But anyway, if he had this with him all the time, there's a chance some of his elemental energy remained on it. D'you think that might come in handy?

talks.objective: Use Elemental Sight to find clues in the diary

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Here we are! This seems to be somewhere that Tejima visited a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The soil looks like it's been disturbed... Maybe Tejima buried something precious here — something that's kept him in the village all these years?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Must be something pretty amazing if it made him stick around for 30 years. Let's dig it up and take a look~!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like... a letter? The paper's gone yellow — must have been written a really long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Konda Village"... Sounds so familiar — where is that place, again?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So the reason Tejima came here was to wait for someone?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But he's been here for 30 years... Aw, guess they didn't show up in the end, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, let's go give Tejima his stuff back and take it from there.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Well, I'll be... That's certainly my handwriting... and I guess the omamori and letter belong to me too.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: ...But I have no memory of anything that's written in this diary.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Still... it's clear that I was waiting for someone here, and that I chose to wait for 30 years.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Over the years, I must have made a note of anything interesting... anything that I could share with her when we were finally reunited.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: And just look at all the things that did happen over the years... The time has flown by so quickly. 30 years feels like the blink of an eye.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: How could I have forgotten something so important to me? Hmm... Now that I think about it, when my Vision was taken from me, it felt like I'd suddenly been... hollowed out.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Love, regret... everything I felt for her... it's all disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Does that make you feel sad?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: No... not especially.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: After all, I've forgotten who she was. Her face, her voice, the things we experienced together... I barely recall any of it.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: It's as if she'd never been in my life to begin with... as if, all these years have been nothing but a hazy dream.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, do you still plan on leaving?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Mm... I think... maybe not. If this is something I waited most of my life for, I suppose I should carry on waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: Although, what if she were to turn up eventually, only to find I didn't remember so much as her name... Wouldn't that be upsetting for her?

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: When I think about it like that... I do feel a slight tinge of sadness in my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: How curious... Why am I thinking like this when I don't even remember who she is? It's just like that feeling of emptiness, the feeling that something is... missing...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: *sigh* Thank you both for helping me reconnect with my reason for staying here.

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I shall remain here, and keep waiting for her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tejima seems to be dealing... okay, but still... it makes Paimon really sad...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems it's just like Ayaka and Thoma were saying. If you lose your Vision, you lose all your hopes and dreams, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That certainly explains the state Tejima was in earlier.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: At least we were able to help him... weren't we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* ...Well, let's go find the next person.

choices.text: Losing a reason to feel sad is maybe the saddest thing of all.

dialogues.speaker: Mahiru
dialogues.text: What could be the matter...

dialogues.speaker: Kenjirou
dialogues.text: We can't let him leave while he's in such a bad state...

dialogues.speaker: Tejima
dialogues.text: I'll stay here, and keep waiting for her...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be the place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to Miss Kamisato, the second one who lost their Vision is a samurai from the Tenryou Commission.
